transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer technical support, my name is Liam. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Liam. I'm having terrible Wi-Fi coverage issues in our newly converted loft bedroom. On the ground floor right next to the Hub router we get two hundred megabits, but upstairs in the loft office the speed drops down to barely three megabits and keeps dropping my video conference calls!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can help you evaluate your Wi-Fi mesh placement and signal coverage, Isabel. Let's start with security verification. What is your full name and billing address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Isabel Ward, 38 Richmond Avenue, Bristol, BS6 5EP.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the four-digit security PIN on the account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So what I understand is you have great two-hundred-megabit speeds near the ground floor Hub, but experience severe signal attenuation down to three megabits in your new loft conversion, disrupting your remote work calls, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly it. The builders used foil-backed plasterboard in the roof insulation, which I suspect is blocking the wireless signal.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Do you currently have an S-Net Wi-Fi Booster pod paired with your Hub router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, we received a black mesh booster pod last week, and I plugged it into a socket right up in the loft next to my desk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What color is the small LED light on the front of that booster pod right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Also, does the booster pod have any large metal mirrors or wardrobes sitting directly in front of it on that landing?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, it's on an open hallway skirting board socket with clear line of sight to the stairs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is ideal because open stairwells act as natural vertical conduits for wireless signals.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the stairwell goes straight up to the loft door.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you can monitor all connected devices on the mesh pod through the Network Map on our mobile app.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll download the app to check device connections.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And the booster firmware updates automatically overnight alongside the main Hub.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know maintenance is fully automated.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if you ever need a second booster for the garden patio, you can order one with no added monthly fee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a great option for the summer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And our Wi-Fi guarantee ensures minimum thirty megabits in every room of the home.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, one hundred and eighty-five megabits blows thirty megabits out of the water!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We always aim for maximum throughput wherever possible.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And you certainly delivered that today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is flashing amber slowly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A flashing amber LED indicates the booster pod is placed too far away from the main Hub, meaning the backhaul wireless link between them is weak and dropping packets.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I thought the booster had to be in the room where I needed the Wi-Fi! I've been struggling with dropped client presentations all week!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Mesh pods cannot amplify a signal that has already degraded through two floors of ceilings and foil insulation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Where should I place it then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously a mesh repeater must be placed halfway between the main router and the dead zone so it receives a strong signal to repeat upwards.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So halfway would be on our first-floor landing outside the master bedroom?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. Unplug the booster from the loft and plug it into a wall socket on that first-floor landing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unplugging it from the loft now... Walking down to the first floor... Plugging it into the landing socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me for about forty seconds while the mesh pod establishes an encrypted 5GHz backhaul link with the Hub.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Isabel. What is the LED on the booster doing now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It flashed green for a few seconds, and now it has turned solid white!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A solid white light confirms a high-throughput backhaul link exceeding four hundred megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Now let me walk back up to the loft with my laptop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just confirming before you test, you had the laptop connected to the two-hundred-megabit Hub network, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, on the main S-Net home network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Open your laptop in the loft office and run the S-Net speed test.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Running speed test now... Needle is flying... One hundred and eighty-five megabits download and thirty megabits upload!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the first-floor booster pod is relaying full-strength signal directly up into the loft without foil attenuation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an incredible difference. It went from three megabits to one hundred and eighty-five megabits just by moving the plug!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And because it's a seamless mesh, your laptop and phone will switch between the Hub and pod automatically as you move around the house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am so relieved. My video calls will be crystal clear tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your billing email on file, it's isabel dot ward at bristol dot org dot uk, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my email.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will note the optimized mesh location on your account profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Liam, that was such simple and effective advice.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your Wi-Fi that I can assist you with today, Isabel?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Liam, the internet is flying in the loft now. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, Isabel, and have a wonderful day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Liam, goodbye.
